sources.title: Доклад об особенностях климата на территории Российской Федерации за 2024 год
sources.organization: Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring (Roshydromet)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate monitoring for 2024; permafrost active-layer trends for 2005–2024; crop precipitation anomalies relative to 1991–2020.
sources.methodology: Official national climate-monitoring report using station observations, regional aggregates, and permafrost monitoring sites.
sources.limitations: The report does not attribute individual weather events to climate change; permafrost monitoring covers few sites and uneven time series.

sources.title: State Report on the Protection of the Population and Territories of the Russian Federation from Natural and Technogenic Emergencies in 2024
sources.organization: Ministry of the Russian Federation for Civil Defence, Emergencies and Elimination of Consequences of Natural Disasters (EMERCOM)
sources.temporal_coverage: Emergency preparedness, disaster response and impacts recorded in 2024.
sources.methodology: Annual national government report compiling regional emergency preparedness, incident records and response operations.
sources.limitations: Administrative and operational reporting; the cited wildfire and flood-preparedness passages do not assess climate attribution.

sources.title: Second Nationally Determined Contribution of the Russian Federation as part of the implementation of the Paris Agreement
sources.temporal_coverage: Government submission in 2025; includes warming observations since the mid-1970s and adaptation arrangements through 2025.
sources.methodology: Government submission summarizing observed trends, adaptation plans and selected practices.
sources.limitations: Self-reported policies; second-stage plan ended in 2025 and later status was not checked.

sources.title: Heuristic relative assessment of climate risks in Russian regions
sources.organization: Higher School of Economics; article published in Science of the Total Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Current exposure and vulnerability indicators with climate-hazard projections to mid-century under multiple SSP scenarios.
sources.methodology: Publisher abstract describes heuristic regional risk ranking using hazard, exposure and vulnerability indicators.
sources.limitations: Full article was not inspected; the abstract notes incomplete spatial economic data and no quantified damage functions.

sources.title: Adapting to what? Regional climate policy in Russia
sources.organization: Fridtjof Nansen Institute; article published in Energy Policy
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional adaptation policies analyzed in an article published online 17 April 2026.
sources.methodology: Publisher abstract summarizes regional climate adaptation policies, including Yamal-Nenets.
sources.limitations: Only the publisher abstract was inspected; no independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Climate risks
sources.temporal_coverage: Bank of Russia climate-risk analysis, stress tests and financial-institution survey reported through 2024; one modeled horizon is 2030–2040.
sources.methodology: Official central-bank page summarizing climate-risk analysis, stress tests and a survey of financial institutions.
sources.limitations: Underlying stress-test and survey reports were not reviewed; the 2030–2040 transition-risk estimates are described as preliminary.

claims.locator: PDF p. 55, section 7 on permafrost active-layer thickness in Western Siberia.
claims.paraphrase: For two monitored sites in Nadym district, Roshydromet reports positive active-layer-thickness trends of 58 and 45 cm per decade over 2005–2024.
claims.limitations: A monitoring result from two sites, not a district-wide infrastructure-damage estimate.

claims.locator: PDF p. 58, Table 8.2 and discussion of 2024 moisture conditions for spring cereals.
claims.paraphrase: Spring-cereal growing-season precipitation in 2024 was 36% below its 1991–2020 normal in the Southern District and 30% below in the North Caucasus; local soil drought was possible in both during June–August.
claims.limitations: Observed 2024 anomaly relative to 1991–2020; the report does not attribute it to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF p. 145, section describing the May 2024 forest fire in the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia).
claims.paraphrase: EMERCOM records May 2024 natural fires over more than 44,271 ha in Yakutia; 2,728 emergency-system personnel and 187 equipment units were mobilized.
institutions: Unified State System for Prevention and Elimination of Emergencies
claims.limitations: Administrative incident and mobilization figures; the report does not attribute the fires to climate change or measure recovery.

claims.locator: PDF p. 159, 2024 checks of regional readiness for the flood-prone period.
claims.paraphrase: Before the 2024 flood season, 48 federal subjects were rated ready and 37 limitedly ready; EMERCOM says the checks prompted revisions to federal and regional emergency plans.
claims.limitations: The cited passage gives aggregate readiness counts without naming the subjects or reporting later flood outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 159, monitoring and operational groups during the 2024 flood-prone period.
claims.paraphrase: During active flood conditions in 2024, 2,499 operational groups were deployed more than 11,100 times, with satellite monitoring received up to seven times daily.
claims.limitations: National deployment totals do not show geographic coverage, warning lead time, or household-level outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 5, National Circumstances, reported surface-temperature trends.
claims.paraphrase: The 2025 submission reports mean annual temperature rising 0.5°C per decade nationally since the mid-1970s and 0.70°C per decade in the Arctic zone, 3.7 times the global rate.
claims.limitations: Government-reported national and Arctic-zone trends; no local impact estimates are given in this passage.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 17–18, adaptation planning system and second-stage action plan.
claims.paraphrase: The submission says first-stage planning ended in 2022; its second-stage plan through 2025 was underway, and regional plus ten sector plans were approved.
claims.limitations: This is the government's 2025 status report; the stated plan period expired and later implementation was not checked.

claims.locator: PDF p. 18, stated tasks of the regional and sectoral adaptation plans.
claims.paraphrase: Plan tasks include reducing climate risks to the traditional livelihoods of Indigenous peoples of the North.
claims.limitations: Stated objective only; no Indigenous community or delivered result is specified.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 18–19, Moscow urban adaptation practices.
claims.paraphrase: The submission reports Moscow prioritizing electricity, heating and gas-network upgrades, alongside planting wind- and frost-resistant trees and increasing irrigation.
claims.limitations: Reported in 2025; no resilience outcome evaluation is provided.

claims.locator: Publisher article page, English abstract, relative regional climate-risk findings.
claims.paraphrase: The abstract's regional ranking places heat and agricultural water stress in southwest Russia, permafrost and fire risks in the northeast, and flood risk in the southeast.
claims.scenario: Exposure and vulnerability indicators use current conditions; hazard indicators project to mid-century under multiple SSP scenarios, whose variants are not specified in the abstract.
claims.limitations: Relative heuristic findings from an abstract; regional directions are broad and not named federal subjects or loss estimates.

claims.locator: FNI publication page, publisher abstract, findings on regional adaptation policy.
claims.paraphrase: The abstract says regional adaptation is often used for modernization, not led by climate policy; mitigation tasks also appear in adaptation plans.
systems: regional adaptation strategies and action plans
claims.limitations: Abstract only; detailed regional evidence was not inspected.

claims.locator: FNI publication page, publisher abstract, Yamal-Nenets case description.
claims.paraphrase: In Yamal-Nenets, adaptation is implemented mainly through sectoral plans embedded in infrastructure, civil protection and resource-management programmes.
claims.limitations: Abstract only; no local outcomes are evaluated.

claims.locator: FNI publication page, opening abstract paragraph on war, sanctions and climate-policy drivers.
claims.paraphrase: The abstract links war and sanctions to a climate-policy setting where domestic politics, not international climate diplomacy, determines Russia's response.
claims.limitations: Abstract-level policy context; no local service mechanism is established.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The publisher abstract places Russia's climate response amid war, sanctions and contracting international cooperation, stating domestic politics rather than international climate diplomacy determines the response.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: FNI publication page, opening abstract paragraph on war, sanctions and climate-policy drivers.

claims.locator: Bank of Russia page, introductory section on physical and transition climate risks.
claims.paraphrase: The Bank says some Russian regions are already experiencing more frequent droughts, floods and other hazards, while export exposure creates transition risks for companies and financial stability.
claims.limitations: The page gives no names of affected regions or local hazard trend series.

claims.locator: Bank of Russia page, section on its 2023 transition-risk stress test.
claims.paraphrase: A 2023 stress test modeled falling demand for carbon-intensive products; without adaptation, mining, quarrying and metallurgy companies could see weaker financial performance in 2030–2040, creating systemic risk.
claims.scenario: Declining demand for carbon-intensive products; the official page does not state scenario magnitudes. Estimates assume no adaptation measures.
claims.limitations: The Bank describes estimates as preliminary; this is modeled transition risk, not an observed climate impact.

claims.locator: Bank of Russia page, section on 2024 survey of financial institutions.
claims.paraphrase: In its 2024 survey, most financial institutions said they factor climate risks into decisions but had not yet adopted more active risk-management approaches.
claims.limitations: The public summary does not report the survey sample size or institution-level differences.

access_audit.locator: Full 139-page Roshydromet report; permafrost section 7 and agrometeorological section 8 inspected.
access_audit.notes: Directly read cited passages in the official publisher PDF, including monitoring limitations and the 1991–2020 crop-weather baseline.

access_audit.locator: Full 272-page 2024 State Report; forest-fire incident and preparedness/monitoring passages inspected.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the official EMERCOM PDF sections supporting the Yakutia fire and 2024 flood-readiness/monitoring figures.

access_audit.locator: Full 44-page Second NDC; national circumstances, adaptation-planning and Moscow practice sections inspected.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the government submission hosted by UNFCCC; historical plan dates and self-reported status are retained.

access_audit.locator: Publisher article page, complete English abstract on risk framework, five risk domains, relative regional pattern and data limitations.
access_audit.notes: Read the publisher page abstract directly; the full journal article was not inspected.

access_audit.locator: FNI publisher page abstract on regional policies, Yamal-Nenets, risks/measures and war/sanctions context.
access_audit.notes: Used only the publisher's abstract summary; direct page rendering required JavaScript and the full article was not inspected.

access_audit.locator: Bank of Russia page sections on regional climate risks, transition stress testing and the 2024 financial-institution survey.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the official web-page body; underlying stress-test and survey reports were not reviewed.

search_audit.query: Russia official and research evidence on regional climate vulnerability: permafrost, agriculture, wildfire, drought, flood and named sites or federal subjects
search_audit.outcome: Read official 2024 climate and emergency reports plus HSE and FNI publisher summaries. Verified named Nadym sites, Yakutia, Moscow and federal-district crop conditions; some scholarly regional profiles remain broad.

search_audit.query: Russia climate change and violent conflict: country-specific climate-to-conflict, violence, displacement, protection or resource-competition pathways
search_audit.outcome: Search and inspected sources did not establish a Russia-specific climate-to-violence or climate-to-armed-conflict pathway. The FNI abstract addresses the ongoing war as policy context, not as a climate-caused outcome.

search_audit.query: Russia war and sanctions effects on regional climate adaptation policy, international climate cooperation and implementation capacity
search_audit.outcome: The publisher abstract for FNI explicitly situates climate response amid war, sanctions and reduced cooperation and says domestic politics, rather than international climate diplomacy, determines the response. No inspected source established a localized conflict-related service or adaptation constraint.

search_audit.query: Russia climate resilience capacity: adaptation plans, Indigenous northern livelihoods, emergency preparedness, early warning and financial-risk management
search_audit.outcome: Read the government NDC and EMERCOM report and official central-bank summary. Plans, response operations and self-reported measures are recorded as capacity or policy evidence, not evaluated resilience outcomes.

gaps: No directly inspected Russia-specific evidence established a climate-to-violent-conflict or climate-to-armed-conflict pathway; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.

Roshydromet's active-layer trends are based on a small, uneven set of permafrost plots; the report says long-term trend estimation requires multi-decade records and some eastern regions lack comparable observations.
The HSE article was used at abstract level only; its broad southwest/northeast/southeast patterns do not name federal subjects and its heuristic rankings are not quantified damage estimates.
The FNI full article was not inspected; the publisher abstract supports only high-level claims about regional policy and its Yamal-Nenets case.
The 2025 Second NDC reports a second-stage adaptation plan running through 2025; post-2025 plan status and implementation were not verified.
EMERCOM 2024 readiness counts and incident figures are historical administrative records, not climate-attribution evidence; aggregate readiness does not identify weaker individual regions.
The Bank of Russia webpage summarizes stress tests and a survey, but underlying methods, sample sizes and local variation were not reviewed.
